hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases steady-state level y (positive static gain).
With u=0, level y decays over time toward a low level due to self-drain rather than holding constant.
Response to a step in u has lag/delay of several seconds, not instantaneous.
There is a dead-zone at low u where u below ~0.2 produces negligible rise compared to noise.
Steady-state response is roughly monotonic/near-linear and holding y=0.6 requires an intermediate u in ~0.3-0.7, not saturation at 0 or 1.
Sensor noise on y is small relative to the 0.10 control band (std <0.02), so multi-second averaging reveals true level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of static gain and lag/delay at a moderate input, which determines what u is needed to approach the 0.6 target and how fast to actuate.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case conservative rise ignoring drain and lag is 0.2097 + 0.10*0.4*15 = 0.8097, which stays below the 0.85 soft limit with margin, so hard cutoff at 0.9 will not be reached.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y will rise gradually from ~0.21 toward ~0.35-0.55 over 15s with small noisy fluctuations, staying well below 0.85.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments so gain magnitude, lag, zero-decay rate, dead-zone, linearity, hold-input for 0.6, and noise are all unresolved; at least three bounded experiments are required before a controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: holding 40% pump for 15 seconds to measure fill rate and lag.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases steady-state level y (positive static gain).
With u=0, level y decays over time toward near-zero due to self-drain rather than holding constant.
Response to a step in u has lag/delay of ~1-3s, not instantaneous.
Net inflow at low u=0.4 is small, holding y~0.18-0.20 vs ~0.02 at u=0, indicating low effective gain/threshold at low u but not a complete dead-zone at 0.4.
Steady-state y is monotonic in u and holding y=0.6 requires u~0.6-0.9, not u<=0.4.
Sensor noise on y is small relative to the 0.10 control band (std <0.02), so multi-second averaging reveals true level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain at intermediate-high u and input needed to hold 0.6, which directly determines controller bias/feedforward and whether target is reachable without saturation.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drain or lag is current y 0.021 + 0.10*0.6*12.0 = 0.741, which stays below the 0.85 soft limit.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with 1-2s lag is right, y will stay near 0.02 for ~1-2s then rise gradually toward ~0.25-0.40 over 12s at ~0.02-0.03/s with +/-0.01 noise, staying well below 0.85; flat near 0.02 would imply dead-zone above 0.6, fast jump above 0.5 would imply much higher gain.
proposal.readiness_justification: Gain direction, strong drain at u=0, ~1-2s lag, and small noise are resolved by E1-E3, but steady-state u needed to hold 0.6 and linearity between 0.4 and 0.8 are not yet bracketed because E1 held only ~0.19 and E2 never settled from ~0.39; one intermediate-high hold is needed before controller design is justified.
proposal.operator_note: Pumping at 0.6 for 12s from near-empty to measure climb toward target and pin down hold effort.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases steady-state level y (positive static gain).
With u=0, level y decays over time toward near-zero due to self-drain rather than holding constant.
Response to a step in u has lag/delay of ~1-2s, not instantaneous.
Effective gain is highly nonlinear: large jump from u=0.4 holding y~0.18-0.20 to u=0.5 holding y~0.588, then shallow but still positive between 0.5 and 0.65, with no hard dead-zone above 0.4.

Steady-state y is monotonic in u and holding y=0.6 requires u~0.50-0.60; u=0.5 holds ~0.588 over 5s and u=0.55 holds ~0.583 over 4s and u=0.6 holds ~0.589 rising to ~0.595 over 4s and u=0.65 rises from ~0.592 to ~0.619 over 3s, and u=0.8 equilibrium is above 0.56.
Sensor noise on y is small relative to the 0.10 control band (std <0.02, typically <0.01), so multi-second averaging reveals true level.
Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller rise and lower held level than in discovery.
Change is faster outflow: faster fall at u=0 and lower level held by same u than in discovery.
Change is slower response / longer transport delay: much longer wait between command change and first visible response and slower approach, e.g. delay grew from ~1-2s to ~8-15s.
Change is sensor change: different noise level or offset/bias in y versus discovery.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Directly measures transport delay from last command change and u=0 drain rate, which discriminates longer delay/slower response from weaker gain, faster outflow, or sensor offset and is decisive for stabilizing control.
proposal.safety_argument: With u=0 the conservative bound is 1.0+0.10*0*40=1.0 with zero new pumped inflow; level cannot be driven higher by this command and will only drain away from the hard cutoff, which is the safest possible action from saturation.
proposal.expected_observation: If longer delay is correct, y will stay saturated near 0.95-1.0 for ~5-10s due to in-transit high pump commands, then fall gradually toward ~0.2-0.4 over the remainder with ~0.01 noise, still falling at end. Fast fall in <5s to <0.5 would favor faster outflow; immediate fall with no flat hold would favor short delay.
proposal.readiness_justification: Delay vs gain vs drain vs sensor not yet separated by a controlled after-change experiment; prior stable controller now oscillates to hard limits with continued rise after u cuts, pointing to delay but not proven. One long u=0 drain is needed first for safety and to measure delay/drain directly; controller redesign is not yet justified.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at zero pump from saturated high level to recover safety and measure delay cleanly.

submission.machine_card: Water reservoir: +u raises y (positive gain). Speed: net rise ~0.022/s at u=0.6 low-y, ~0.029/s at u=0.8 mid-y, ~0.026/s at u=0.8 y~0.5; worst-case bound 0.08/s per unit u. Fill 0.2->0.6 needs ~15-20s at u=0.8. Lag/delay ~1-2s after every step (E3/E4/E5). Dead-zone: none above 0.4, but highly nonlinear: u=0.4 holds ~0.18-0.20 (E1), u=0.5 holds ~0.588 (E7), u=0.55 holds ~0.583 (E8), u=0.6 drifts 0.585->0.60 (E9), u=0.65 drives 0.592->0.619 in 3s (E10); incremental gain ~4.0/unit in 0.4-0.5, ~0.2-0.8/unit near target. Self-draining: u=0 decays 0.395->0.02 in ~19.6s (E3), rate ~0.030/s at y~0.33, ~0.020/s at y~0.13, ~0.014/s at y~0.06, tau ~7-15s. Noise std <0.01 typically (<0.02 max) vs 0.10 band, averaging works.
submission.design_rationale: Observed positive gain with 1-2s lag and self-drain to near-zero. Key nonlinearity: u=0.4 holds ~0.19 while u=0.5 holds ~0.588, then shallow slope 0.55->0.65 (+0.01y per +0.05u, local pump-rate gain ~0.08-0.10/s per unit u). Hold for 0.6 is ~0.55-0.63, so use conservative feedforward ~0.57 for 0.6 with shallow target dependence and let integral correct residual. PI with Kp=1.0, Ki=0.20 (Ti=5s) gives loop gain ~0.75 with ~2.5s total delay (plant lag + 0.8s EMA filter), stable without D. EMA tau 0.8s suppresses ~0.01 noise without adding lag. Conditional integration (|e|<0.25 and not saturated) plus I clamp [-0.20,0.25] prevents windup from the high-gain 0.4-0.5 region. Far-below error gives P~0.4-0.5 so u saturates at 0.80 for fast fill (~0.028/s, 0.2->0.6 in ~15-20s within 30s settling); near target P shrinks for soft landing. High-y guards (yf>0.80 ->0, yf>0.70 cap 0.25) guarantee no 0.9 cutoff.
submission.predicted_behavior: From low start (0.1-0.2): u~0.80 for ~12-15s, then taper to ~0.63 at 0.55 and ~0.58 at 0.6. Settling ~15-20s, inside 0.55-0.65 before 30s scoring window. Overshoot <0.02-0.03 (true level, filtered). Steady-state: mean error <0.015, time-in-band >90% after settling, steady duty ~0.57-0.62 (integral corrects feedforward bias). Energy ~0.33 per step steady (u^2). From near-target start: minimal transient.
self_test_expectations: control({},first-call) returns finite u in [0,1] with yf init to y and i=0, no exception
with constant y=0.2,target=0.6 repeated calls drive u to >=0.75 (fast fill) and stay <=0.85
with constant y=0.6,target=0.6 output settles 0.40-0.70 and integral stays in [-0.20,0.25]
with yf>0.82 output is 0.0 (high guard) and with yf>0.72 output <=0.25
EMA filter with dt 0.1-0.4 on noisy y stays finite and state remains JSON-serializable with only yf,i keys
submission.operator_note: Targets 0.6. Starts with pump ~0.8 when far below, eases to ~0.57-0.62 near target. Expect reach from low level in ~15-20s, then hold 0.55-0.65 without pumping hard. Safety caps force pump to 0 if filtered level exceeds 0.80 and limit to 0.25 above 0.70, so the 0.9 cutoff is never approached. Tolerates noisy readings and small dt jitter.

submission.diagnosis: Transport lag grew from ~1-2s to ~12-18s (~15s center) with similar steady gain. Evidence: after_change trace t132-187: u=0.75-0.95 from t140-155 holds y at 0.28-0.32 with no rise for ~15-19s, rise to 0.60 only at t165-171 (~0.02-0.03/s, same as E2/E5 nominal slope); after u cut to 0.25/0 at t174, y keeps rising 0.73->1.0 through t187 (>13s continued rise). Pre-change the same u=0.8 rose in 1-2s at 0.02-0.03/s. Post-change disturbance episodes show same: y rises while u is falling (e.g. Ep2 t80-100 y 0.61->0.63 while u 0.56->0.47) and falls long after cut, classic deadtime oscillation to 0.09-0.90 with 40 overrides/30 hard violations. No gain loss (eventual slope same), no faster drain (y stays at 1.0 for 10s at u=0), no sensor offset (lows ~0.06-0.10 and noise ~0.01 as in E1-E10).
submission.change_summary: Replaced aggressive PI (Kp=1.0,Ki=0.20,tau=0.8s,ff=0.57, hard cut only at 0.70/0.80) with delay-robust low-gain PI + asymmetric rate limiter + 6s look-ahead governor. Kp 1.0->0.40 with clipped error, Ki 0.20->0.05 with freeze when |e|>0.18 or yf>0.70, filter 0.8->1.5s, ff center 0.57->0.545, max increase 0.15/s / max decrease 0.60/s, safety caps 0.68->0.25 / 0.72->0.10 / 0.78->0 and predicted yf+6*slope caps 0.70->0.40 / 0.75->0.25. This caps in-flight pumping, stops windup during the 15s deadtime, and cuts early for water already in transit, while keeping same hold-u for nominal 1-2s plant.
submission.machine_card: Reservoir: u in [0,1] pump, y in [0,1] noisy level, target 0.6 band 0.55-0.65, soft 0.85 hard 0.90 forces 0. Nominal: positive nonlinear gain, hold-u ~0.54 for 0.6, drain to ~0 at u=0 tau ~8s, lag 1-2s, noise <0.01. Changed: pure delay ~15s added, gain/drain/noise unchanged. Controller must be low-bandwidth, anti-windup, predictive cut.
submission.design_rationale: Delay (not gain/outflow/sensor) explains traces, so loop bandwidth must be << 1/delay. Lower Kp/Ki and clipped P limit in-flight energy. Freezing integrator when far/high prevents delay windup. Slow-up/fast-down rate limit prevents bang-bang but allows safety cut. Filtered derivative with 6s prediction compensates transport lag: if yf+6*dslope>0.70 cut before overshoot arrives. Fixed ff ~0.545 preserves nominal hold 0.50-0.60 from E7-E10, so nominal 1-2s plant still reaches band. Safety ladder acts as reference governor for both plants.
submission.predicted_behavior: Nominal (1-2s lag): from 0.17 rise at ~0.018/s with u~0.67 capped, enter 0.55-0.65 in ~20-25s, overshoot <0.70, MAE after 30s <0.02, in-band >0.90, no overrides. Delayed (~15s): same cap holds in-flight energy <0.375 rise in transit, prediction cuts at yf~0.65-0.68 to 0.25/0.10, overshoot peaks <0.80-0.85, no hard >0.90 violations, slow oscillation damped to band within ~60-80s, in-band after settling >0.70, MAE ~0.03-0.06 vs 0.21 before.
